baseline.description: Predict log1p Cu from 50 nearest retained training sites in EPSG:3005 with inverse-squared-distance weights. Break distance ties by sample ID. If fewer than 50 training sites, stop. Exact zero distance uses mean of zero-distance training targets. Fixed k=50 transferred from earlier US soil work; no tuning on BC scores.

candidates.configuration: Fit a mean log1p Cu per source rock_class with shrinkage of 20 pseudo-observations at the overall training mean: (sum_class + 20*globalMean)/(n_class+20). Unknown/unseen class uses the global training mean. Compute training residuals from those class means. Predict class mean plus the same 50-neighbor inverse-squared-distance weighted residuals. Clip predicted log1p Cu below zero to zero. No hyperparameter search.
candidates.description: Mapped geology class mean plus spatially interpolated training residuals

limitations: Registry events make protocol and exposure history inspectable; they are not model improvements.

New audit starts require archived source, normalized data, evaluator code, model, validation predictions and sealed audit predictions matching frozen identities and memberships. Generic file and row checks alone do not validate scientific execution.

The BC adapter reproduces source normalization, fixed training-only models and sealed predictions before a single score attempt. It applies only to its reviewed retrospective protocol; other sources require adapters. No automatic promotion or learned research policy is connected.
The hash chain detects changed events relative to its published head. A filesystem owner can rewrite local history; external published checkpoints are needed to detect full-chain replacement.

Audit reservations conservatively apply to the entire raw source release, across targets and normalization versions. Repackaging/renaming records can defeat raw-hash and ID-only overlap checks; a source-specific lineage review remains necessary. No reset or reuse operation is provided.
